full_text: 2026 MEDI-CAL NEW MEMBER GUIDE. CONTENTS: Message from L.A. Care 1, Important Changes to Medi-Cal 2, Medi-Cal Renewal 5, Where to Go for Care 6, Behavioral Health Services & Care 9, Prepare for Your Doctor Visit 10, Getting Started as a Member 12, Benefit Highlights 16, VSP Vision Care 18, Virtual Care Options 19, Medi-Cal Rx and Transportation 20, Community Resource Centers and Community Link 21, Health Education Services 22, My Health In Motion 24, How to Access Member Materials 25, Reporting Problems, Important Numbers and Stay Connected 26, Language Assistance 27, Nondiscrimination Notice 29. Dear L.A. Care Member, Welcome to L.A. Care Health Plan (L.A. Care). L.A. Care is the largest Medi-Cal plan in California that provides health care coverage to Medi-Cal beneficiaries residing in Los Angeles County. IMPORTANT UPCOMING CHANGES to Medi-Cal Eligibility and Benefits: Starting January 1, 2026, some adult immigrants will no longer be able to sign up for full-scope Medi-Cal coverage based on their immigration status (Enrollment Freeze). ASSET LIMITS: Starting January 1, 2026, when you apply for or renew your Medi-Cal, we will look at what you own (asset check). The most you can own (asset limit) is $130,000 for one person. DENTAL COVERAGE CHANGES: Starting July 1, 2026, some adult immigrant Medi-Cal members aged 19 or older will stop getting full-scope dental services. WORK RULES: Starting January 1, 2027, some childless adults enrolled in Medi-Cal will be required to engage in community service, work (paid employment), or other qualifying activities 80 hours per month. 6-MONTH ELIGIBILITY CHECKS: Starting January 1, 2027, some Medi-Cal members will have their eligibility checked twice a year. MONTHLY PREMIUMS: Starting July 1, 2027, some Medi-Cal members who do not have a satisfactory immigration status will need to pay a small monthly fee (premium). COPAYMENTS: Starting October 1, 2028, some Medi-Cal members may need to pay a small fee (copayment)
